steps.action:
# The Last Light

Every night, Thomas climbed 112 steps to light the lamp.

He had counted them the first night, thirty years ago. He counted them still — not because he'd forgotten, but because counting meant he wasn't alone.

Ships passed without knowing his name. That was fine. They passed *safely*. That was everything.

On the night of the great storm, when the wind screamed and the sea swallowed the horizon whole, Thomas climbed his steps — *one, two, three* — and kept the light burning with shaking hands.

In the morning, three vessels sat safely in the harbor.

None of them ever knew.

Thomas descended his 112 steps, made coffee, and smiled.
